Flow: Temple trusts and construction donations. Stated purpose: The donations are stated to fund temple building and upkeep.. How it controls: Trust boards are drawn from prominent donor families, and donor prestige hierarchies shape influence.. Who benefits: Trust boards and prominent donor families benefit..
Temple trusts and construction donations

Flow: Auctioned ritual honors (bidding for rites). Stated purpose: The auctions are stated to support the temple through devotion.. How it controls: They are an explicit purchase of religious status, with wealth converted directly into sanctity.. Who benefits: Temples benefit, and so does the status of winning families..
Auctioned ritual honors (bidding for rites)

Flow: Monastic support and event sponsorship. Stated purpose: Sponsorship is stated to sustain ascetics.. How it controls: Sponsorship is public and ranked, which puts status pressure on families of modest means.. Who benefits: Monastic orders benefit, as do the reputations of sponsoring families..
Monastic support and event sponsorship

Flow: Community business networks and credit. Stated purpose: The networks are stated to provide mutual commercial trust.. How it controls: Religious standing and creditworthiness become the same thing, so dissent is economically expensive.. Who benefits: Established merchant families benefit. PATTERN OBSERVED.
